title: 1990 Paris–Dakar Rally
who: Won by Ari Vatanen (Peugeot) and Edi Orioli (Cagiva)
summary: The 1990 edition of the Dakar Rally, in its African era: 21 stage towns and bivouacs through France, Libya, Niger, Chad, Mali, Mauritania, Senegal. Winners — Cars: Ari Vatanen (Peugeot); Bikes: Edi Orioli (Cagiva).
approximate: Stage towns and bivouacs from Wikipedia's stage table. The rally ran off-road between them, so the lines are straight from bivouac to bivouac.

stops.name: Chevilly
stops.text: A 5 km prologue near Paris for the 12th Dakar, with 465 competitors.

stops.name: Marseille
stops.text: A second short prologue, 3.5 km, before the crossing to Libya.

stops.name: Tripoli
stops.text: Stage 1 starts in Tripoli, the first Dakar to run through Libya.

stops.name: Ghadamès
stops.text: Stage 1: 273 km timed, in the dunes where the Mitsubishis lost ground to Peugeot.

stops.name: Ghat
stops.text: Stage 2: a 609 km special south along the Algerian border.

stops.name: Sabha
stops.text: Stage 3: 446 km timed to Sabha.

stops.name: Tumu
stops.text: Stage 4: 641 km to the Libya–Niger border.

stops.name: Dirkou
stops.text: Stage 5: 504 km through the Ténéré to the Dirkou oasis.

stops.name: N'Gourti
stops.text: Stage 6: 497 km south towards Lake Chad.

stops.name: N'Djamena
stops.text: Stage 7: 499 km into Chad, to the capital.

stops.name: N'Guigmi
stops.text: Stage 8: 425 km back into Niger.

stops.name: Agadez
stops.text: Stage 9, at 780 km the longest special, then a rest day in Agadez.

stops.name: Tahoua
stops.text: Stage 10: 198 km timed.

stops.name: Niamey
stops.text: Stage 11: 222 km timed to Niger's capital.

stops.name: Gao
stops.text: Stage 12: 492 km into Mali.

stops.name: Tombouctou
stops.text: Stage 13: 412 km up the Niger to Timbuktu.

stops.name: Néma
stops.text: Stage 14: 674 km into Mauritania.

stops.name: Tidjikja
stops.text: Stage 15: 458 km across the Mauritanian desert.

stops.name: Kayes
stops.text: Stage 16: 485 km south into Mali.

stops.name: Saint Louis
stops.text: Stage 17 into Senegal, 838 km in all.

stops.name: Dakar
stops.text: The finish after a 40 km last special. Ari Vatanen led a Peugeot 1-2-3 in the 405 T16, his third win in four years; Edi Orioli won the bikes on a Cagiva Elefant.
